title: Bonus: Programs That Talk Back
story: Every program so far has only talked. Real programs also listen: a quiz asks for your name, a game asks for a move. That input arrives on standard input, and XIOM reads it with io.read_line() and io.read_int().
why: Input turns a script into a conversation. It is how a program takes a name, a number, or a choice from the person using it, and how it stays useful when the values are not known in advance.
analogy: Standard input is a mailbox: the program reads one letter (line) at a time, always from the top of the pile. When the mailbox is empty, a read returns nothing instead of waiting forever.
try_it: Change the program to read a third line and print it in uppercase, or read two numbers and print their sum.
tips: `io.read_line()` strips the trailing newline, so the text is ready to compare or join
`io.read_int()` and `io.read_float()` parse one whole line; a read past the end returns `Err` (and `read_line` returns "")
One value per line keeps sample input simple: `Ada` on the first line, `36` on the second
common_mistakes: Expecting `read_line()` to include the newline - it does not
Reading a number with `read_line()`: the result stays text, so use `io.read_int()` / `io.read_float()`
Forgetting the Input box: with no input every read returns empty text or `Err`
